So S = p-(vinyl)phenyl... S = 4-(prop-1-en-... ) Actually S = 1-(4-vinylphenyl)ethanol? Hmm then BH3 hydroboration of alkene gives -CH(OH)CH3 on ring: T = 1-(4-(1-hydroxyethyl)phenyl)ethanol — two stereocenters, symmetric molecule? The two CH(OH)CH3 groups identical → meso possible: stereoisomers = 3 (RR, SS, RS meso). Statement 1: stereocentres = 2 ✓. Statement 2: stereoisomers = 2 ✗ (3). Statement 6: S decolourises bromine water — S has alkene (vinyl) ✓. Correct: 1,3,5,6 = 4.

Hmm but maybe Zn gives ethyl (dehalogenation) making S = 4-ethyl... then no alkene, S wouldn't decolourise, and BH3 on what? S must have alkene for BH3. So S = vinyl. Answer 4.
